findings.title: totalPages off-by-one adds an empty page when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body:
`totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and a limit of 50 it reports 2 pages, and with 100 members it reports 3.

The Next button stays enabled. Clicking it sets offset to `user_count`, and the server returns an empty member list, so the admin sees a blank last page (e.g. "2/2" with no members).

The same happens after removing the only member on the last page: `findMembers` reloads with the old offset, the page comes back empty, and it still counts as a valid page.

Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` instead. Also clamp `offset` to the last real page after a removal.

findings.title: Public group members page now shows only the first 50 members with no way to page
findings.body:
The public `/groups/:name/members` page now calls `model.findMembers()`, which uses the model default `limit: 50, offset: 0`. The `group/members.hbs` template only iterates `members` and has no next/previous controls.

Previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups returned 200. Now any group with more than 50 members is silently truncated to 50 on the public page, and users cannot reach the rest.

Either add pagination or infinite loading to the public template, or keep requesting enough members there.

findings.title: remove_member uses users.delete which bypasses GroupUser destroy callbacks
findings.body:
`group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` deletes the `group_users` join rows with a SQL `delete_all`. It does not destroy them, so GroupUser `after_destroy` callbacks (title/primary-group cleanup) never run. The `user_count` counter cache may also not be maintained, and this PR now displays that count and uses it for pagination.

The previous code path used `group.remove(user)`, which destroys each GroupUser and runs those callbacks. Removed users can therefore keep stale group-derived state (title, primary group), and `user_count` can drift.

Look up the user and call `group.remove(user)` instead. The trailing `group.save` is also unnecessary.

findings.title: Removing nested group params and PATCH changes API silently breaks existing clients (and hides groups)
findings.body:
The admin groups API changed incompatibly:
- `create` now reads `params[:name]` instead of `params[:group][:name]`.
- `update` reads top-level params instead of `params[:group]`.
- The PATCH `changes: {add:, delete:}` incremental membership API is gone.

Existing API integrations (e.g. SSO/sync scripts) get a bad failure mode. A PUT with `group[...]`, or a PATCH with `changes`, now hits `update`, where `params[:visible]` is absent. So `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` sets the group to invisible, the request returns success, and no membership change happens. Creates with nested params fail with an empty name.

Consider keeping backward compatibility, or at least not resetting `visible` when the param is absent.

findings.title: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded limit and negative offset
findings.body:
`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to SQL without validation, on an endpoint any visitor can call for visible groups.

- A huge `limit` (e.g. 1000000 on the trust_level_0 automatic group) serializes the whole user base in one request.
- A negative limit or offset makes PostgreSQL raise ("OFFSET must not be negative"), which surfaces as a 500.

Clamp `limit` to a sane maximum and offset/limit to be non-negative.

findings.title: members.json response shape changed from array to object without updating/adding specs
findings.body:
`GET /groups/:name/members.json` used to return a JSON array of users. It now returns `{members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}`, which breaks any external consumer of this public endpoint.

No spec covers the new response shape or the pagination behaviour (limit/offset/total), so regressions in the meta values the admin pager depends on would go unnoticed.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses PUT although the route is DELETE
findings.body:
The test "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`.

Controller specs dispatch straight to the action and don't enforce the HTTP verb, so the test passes while not exercising the real request. Use `xhr :delete` to match the route and the other remove_member test.
